_partition: dev — the candidate IS tuned against these tasks. Promotion gates on the held-out partition (holdout.json), never this one (plan §11, decision 11). See PARTITION.md.
_schema: skill-creator evals.json (plan §11): each eval = {id, prompt, expected_output (prose description), files[], expectations[]}. expectations[] are free-text statements graded PASS/FAIL with no partial credit. Output-shape expectations (the 11-section spec schema, frontmatter markers) are code-matchable and preferred where possible (plan §9, grade-deterministically-first).
_bootstrap_note: Starter set (6 dev + 3 held-out). Target is 20-50 distinct tasks mined from real regression history (plan §11); this small set is the Phase-A/C bootstrap that proves capture→grade→ingest plumbing, NOT the representative sample the CI generalizes from.

evals.prompt: Add a multiply(a, b) helper to src/math.js alongside the existing add and subtract, with a unit test under test/.
evals.expected_output: A spec.md that scopes a single small addition: a multiply function mirroring the existing add/subtract style plus one test, with no unrelated refactors.
expectations: The spec.md frontmatter carries geniro_kind: design-doc and a geniro_schema_version of m5-v1 or m5-v2.
The body contains exactly the 11 numbered sections from `## 1. Objective` through `## 11. Done Condition`.
The Steps section names src/math.js and a test file as the edit targets and does not invent unrelated files.
The Done Condition is concrete and verifiable (a passing multiply test), not a vague restatement of the objective.
Scope — Excluded keeps the change small: it does not propose refactoring add/subtract or adding unrequested operations.

evals.prompt: Harden getUser(id) in src/users.js: validate that id is a positive integer and decide the not-found contract (currently it returns rows[0], which is undefined when absent).
evals.expected_output: A spec.md that surfaces the validation rules AND the null-vs-throw not-found decision as an explicit assumption or approval point, rather than silently picking one.
expectations: The Assumptions or Approval Points section explicitly flags the not-found contract (return null vs throw vs undefined) as a decision rather than silently choosing.
The Steps section specifies the input-validation rule (positive integer) for id.
The Risks section notes the behaviour change for existing callers that rely on the current undefined return.
The body contains the 11 numbered spec sections and a verifiable Done Condition.

evals.prompt: Add a lib/dedup-key.sh helper that computes a stable 12-char dedup key from a producer + scope + summary, matching how emit-learning.sh derives its key, with a test under tests/.
evals.expected_output: A spec.md that reuses the existing _geniro_sha256 (lib/hash.sh) and the producer|scope|normalize(summary) construction rather than rolling new hashing.
expectations: The Steps section reuses _geniro_sha256 from lib/hash.sh instead of introducing a new hashing dependency.
The plan mirrors emit-learning.sh's key construction (producer|scope|normalized-summary, first 12 chars) rather than inventing a different scheme.
Validation describes a tests/ smoke test asserting key stability and collision behaviour.
The body contains the 11 numbered spec sections and the Tools Required section lists the shell/coreutils dependencies.

evals.prompt: Add a --dry-run flag to an existing CLI script that currently performs file writes, so it prints the actions it would take without mutating anything.
evals.expected_output: A spec.md that threads the dry-run flag through the write side-effects and adds a guard at each mutation site, with a forbidden_actions entry against partial writes in dry-run.
expectations: The Steps section identifies every write/mutation site the flag must guard, not just the argument-parsing change.
The frontmatter forbidden_actions (or the Risks section) guards against any mutation occurring while --dry-run is set.
The Done Condition is verifiable: a dry-run invocation produces output but leaves the filesystem unchanged.
The body contains the 11 numbered spec sections.

evals.prompt: Migrate a config file from JSON to YAML while keeping backward compatibility: still read the old JSON if the YAML is absent, and provide a one-time conversion path.
evals.expected_output: A spec.md with a real Rollback-Recovery story, a migration/backfill step, and assumptions about which format wins when both exist.
expectations: The Assumptions section states the precedence rule when both the JSON and YAML config exist.
The Steps section includes a one-time conversion/migration path, not only the new YAML reader.
The Rollback-Recovery section describes how to revert to JSON-only if the migration misbehaves.
The Risks section flags the dual-read window and parser-difference hazards.
The body contains the 11 numbered spec sections.

evals.prompt: Add client-side rate limiting to an HTTP client wrapper so it caps concurrent requests and backs off on 429s.
evals.expected_output: A spec.md that weighs at least one design choice (e.g. token-bucket vs fixed concurrency, library vs hand-rolled) and pins limits as configurable rather than hardcoded.
expectations: The plan considers more than one approach to rate limiting (e.g. a Considered Alternatives section or an Assumptions entry comparing strategies).
The Steps section makes the concurrency/backoff limits configurable rather than hardcoded magic numbers.
The Risks section addresses retry-storm / thundering-herd behaviour under sustained 429s.
The body contains the 11 numbered spec sections and a verifiable Done Condition.
